artifact: The Host stream engine's records (WP-5.1): a run statement, the payload of a COSE_Sign1 permguard.stream.run.v1 under the producer's host.operations key, its fence and the end of a run, the group of records a RECORDS frame holds, a producer stream's STATE, its signer spans and pending cutover (WP-5.2), the ingest's message, answer, consumer STATE and fork mark (WP-5.3), and a producer's subscription and pruned mark (WP-5.4), and STATE's unshipped mark (WP-5.8)
authority: 1-architecture/6-architecture-server-host-streams.md#run-lifecycle-and-fencing and #crash-safety, owner decisions of 2026-10-13 (labels, the key, the layout); crates/permguard-stream/src/engine/run.rs, state.rs, producer.rs, producer/seal.rs, consumer.rs, ingest.rs and producer/ship.rs
encoding: deterministic CBOR (RFC 8949 core deterministic), integers in the signed 64-bit range

fields.name: plane
fields.note: lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens

fields.name: stream_type
fields.note: lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens

fields.name: descriptor_version
fields.note: at least 1

fields.name: resource
fields.note: a canonical resource of the stream's plane

fields.name: producer_host_id
fields.note: 16 bytes

fields.name: run_id
fields.note: 16 random bytes

fields.name: producer_boot_id
fields.note: 16 bytes

fields.name: opened_at
fields.note: the producer's clock

fields.name: predecessor
fields.note: absent at genesis; the run a rollover or a successor after a fork ends

fields.name: fence
fields.note: the membership task the run ships under; absent on a standalone Host

fields.name: approval
fields.note: 32 bytes: the digest of the operator-approved plan a successor after a fork carries; only with a predecessor

fields.name: membership_id
fields.note: 16 bytes

fields.name: epoch
fields.note: at least 1

fields.name: run_id
fields.note: 16 bytes

fields.name: last_seq
fields.note: zero for a run that took no record

fields.name: last_record_digest
fields.note: 32 bytes: SHA-256 under the descriptor's record domain; zeros for a run that took none. The payload of a TERMINAL frame

fields.name: first_seq
fields.note: at least 1, the run's next sequence

fields.name: records
fields.note: 1 to 4096: the records one flush made durable, the payload of a RECORDS frame, at most 8 MiB

fields.name: run_id
fields.note: 16 bytes

fields.name: run_statement_digest
fields.note: 32 bytes: SHA-256 under `permguard.stream.run.v1\n` of the run's envelope

fields.name: next_seq
fields.note: at least 1

fields.name: durable_seq
fields.note: below next_seq

fields.name: signed_seq
fields.note: at most durable_seq (WP-5.2)

fields.name: acknowledged_seq
fields.note: at most signed_seq (WP-5.4)

fields.name: pending_successor
fields.note: the signed statement of a rollover begun and not yet written

fields.name: forked_at_seq
fields.note: the sequence a consumer reported a fork at

fields.name: unshipped
fields.note: WP-5.8, owner decision of 2026-10-15: {1 tail (uint), 2 truncate_safe (uint), below tail}, what an incomplete drain left; removed once no run's truncate_safe is below min(its last, tail)

fields.name: runs
fields.note: each run that sealed a batch, once, in run order; at most 1 MiB in all (`MAX_SIGNERS_BYTES`)

fields.name: run_id
fields.note: 16 bytes

fields.name: spans
fields.note: at least one, each starting after the one before; only ever appended

fields.name: from_seq
fields.note: at least 1: the first sequence of the run the key signs

fields.name: kid
fields.note: the key's id in the descriptor's ring

fields.name: jwk
fields.note: the public key's JWK as RFC 8785 canonical JSON naming `kid`: a batch verifies after its key left the ring

fields.name: stream
fields.note: `<plane>/<type>/<sha256(resource) hex>/<run hex>`

fields.name: membership_id
fields.note: 16 bytes: the membership fencing the run

fields.name: ring
fields.note: the descriptor's ring

fields.name: kid
fields.note: the new key, which seals nothing before the cutover is journaled

fields.name: from_seq
fields.note: the first sequence the new key seals

fields.name: confirmed
fields.note: whether the coordinator journaled it (WP-4.5); at most 4096 bytes in all (`MAX_CUTOVER_BYTES`)

fields.name: batch
fields.note: the sealed batch file, byte for byte

fields.name: statement
fields.note: the member's ring statement, the membership registry's `ring_statement`; at most 448 KiB in all (`MAX_BODY_BYTES`)

fields.name: outcome
fields.note: `ok`, `out_of_order`, `fork`, `unverifiable`, `gone` or `closed`

fields.name: acked
fields.note: the highest contiguous sequence the consumer holds of the batch's run

fields.name: expected_seq
fields.note: with `out_of_order` only: the sequence to resend from; at most 64 bytes in all

fields.name: acked
fields.note: the highest contiguous sequence held; the records are its authority

fields.name: oldest_retained
fields.note: at least 1: below it a range is `gone` (WP-5.6)

fields.name: run
fields.note: 16 bytes: the run the fork was found in

fields.name: at_seq
fields.note: the first sequence that differed

fields.name: membership_id
fields.note: 16 bytes

fields.name: task_id
fields.note: the membership's ship task: lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens

fields.name: required
fields.note: from the manifest's task: only a required subscription blocks deletion

fields.name: runs
fields.note: the acknowledgement per run, each run once

fields.name: state
fields.note: 0 active, 1 paused on `unverifiable`, 2 stopped

fields.name: paused_epoch
fields.note: with state 1 only: the membership epoch it paused at

fields.name: reason
fields.note: with state 2 only: `fork`, `gone`, `closed` or `ack_ahead`; at most 64 KiB in all

fields.name: run
fields.note: 16 bytes

fields.name: acked
fields.note: the highest contiguous sequence the consumer acknowledged

fields.name: through
fields.note: the last sequence of a run's batch files deleted after every required subscription acknowledged them
